stories.title: Bitcoin's BIP-110 soft fork enters mandatory signaling with miner support under 3%
stories.summary: A contested Bitcoin Improvement Proposal, BIP-110, entered its mandatory signaling phase at block 961,632, according to CoinDesk and Cointelegraph. Miner support for the proposal is running below 3%, well short of the broad consensus soft forks typically need to activate cleanly.
stories.whyItMatters: Thin miner buy-in for a live signaling attempt is a live test of how Bitcoin's governance handles contested protocol changes, with implications for network stability if the attempt stalls or splits opinion.
whatToWatch: Whether miner signaling support rises before any activation deadline
Statements from core developers or major mining pools on the proposal
Whether the signaling attempt is allowed to run its course or is abandoned
questions: What happens to the fork attempt if the signaling threshold is never met?
Who is driving BIP-110 and what problem is it meant to solve?

stories.title: BIP-110 fork attempt mines two blocks, then stalls
stories.summary: A day after mandatory signaling began with miner support under 3%, the BIP-110 soft-fork attempt mined two blocks before stopping, CoinDesk reports. No further detail on the cause was provided.
stories.whyItMatters: An early stall so soon after launch suggests the low miner support seen at signaling translated directly into the attempt losing momentum, a useful data point on how contested Bitcoin protocol changes fare in practice.
whatToWatch: Whether proponents restart or formally abandon the attempt
Any technical post-mortem from developers on why it stopped
questions: Was the stoppage a technical failure or a deliberate pause?
Does this effectively end the BIP-110 push?

stories.title: Bitcoin and Ether ETFs pull in over $1B in their best week since April, with BlackRock taking 80%
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs combined took in more than $1 billion over the week, their strongest week since April, per CryptoSlate. BlackRock's funds captured roughly 80% of that inflow, far outpacing rival issuers.
stories.whyItMatters: Weekly ETF flows remain one of the clearest read-outs of institutional demand for crypto exposure, and the concentration in one issuer says something about where big allocators are choosing to route money.
whatToWatch: Whether next week's flow data sustains or reverses the rebound
Whether other issuers narrow BlackRock's share of inflows
questions: What specifically drove the pickup in demand this week?
How much of the flow is new money versus rotation between funds?

sources.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs break $1B in their best week since April and BlackRock brought in 80% of the cash

stories.title: BTCPay Server restricts remote Lightning access after attackers steal funds
stories.summary: BTCPay Server has locked down remote access to its Lightning Network functionality after attackers exploited it to steal funds, according to Cointelegraph. The report did not specify the scale of losses or the exact vulnerability used.
stories.whyItMatters: BTCPay is widely used self-hosted payment infrastructure for Bitcoin merchants, so a theft-driven lockdown of its Lightning access is a concrete security incident for anyone relying on it for payments.
whatToWatch: Official disclosure of losses and the attack vector
Whether a patch or permanent fix follows the restriction
questions: How much was actually stolen?
Is the restriction temporary or a lasting change to how remote Lightning access works?

sources.title: BTCPay restricts remote Lightning access after attackers steal funds

stories.title: Bitcoin, XRP, Solana and Tron have outpaced Ethereum and Cardano in investor buying every month since 2022
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Bitcoin, XRP, Solana and Tron have beaten Ethereum and Cardano on investor buying in every single month going back to 2022, per its analysis.
stories.whyItMatters: A multi-year pattern in relative demand across large-cap tokens is a signal for how investor preference among major chains has shifted, beyond any single month's noise.
whatToWatch: Whether Ethereum or Cardano interrupt the streak in coming months
Any catalysts (ETF approvals, upgrades) that could shift the pattern
questions: What exact metric is being used to define "investor buying" here?
Does this reflect retail flows, institutional flows, or both?

stories.title: US spot Bitcoin ETFs post $1B inflow week, best since April
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs logged roughly $1 billion in net inflows over the week, their strongest showing since April, according to Cointelegraph.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin ETF flows are a primary gauge of institutional appetite, and a best-in-months week is worth tracking against recent softer periods.
whatToWatch: Whether the pace of inflows holds into next week's data
How this week's total compares issuer-by-issuer
questions: What triggered the acceleration in inflows this particular week?

stories.title: Bitcoin's first 'institutional bear market' takes shape as liquidity drains
stories.summary: CryptoSlate argues Bitcoin is showing early signs of its first bear market driven primarily by institutional dynamics, with liquidity draining from the market. Separately, the outlet reported that an AI-driven security sprint aimed at Bitcoin's ecosystem flagged 6,700 potential issues in 55 hours, though it's unclear how many of those findings are genuine vulnerabilities.
stories.whyItMatters: A liquidity-driven downturn led by institutional behavior would mark a different dynamic than past retail-driven Bitcoin bear markets, and the scale of the AI security sprint's findings raises questions about signal versus noise in automated vulnerability hunting.
whatToWatch: Further liquidity and flow data confirming or denying the bear-market thesis
Triage results on how many of the 6,700 flagged issues are validated as real
questions: What specifically distinguishes this as an "institutional" bear market?
How many of the AI-flagged issues will turn out to be false positives?

stories.title: Senate to vote on advancing crypto market-structure CLARITY Act in September
stories.summary: Senate Majority Leader Thune has filed cloture on the CLARITY Act, setting up a vote to advance the crypto market-structure bill in September, according to Cointelegraph.
stories.whyItMatters: CLARITY Act is a central piece of pending US crypto market-structure legislation, and a scheduled cloture vote is a concrete step toward (or away from) regulatory clarity the industry has been waiting on.
whatToWatch: The September cloture vote outcome
Any amendments or negotiated changes ahead of the vote
questions: Does the bill currently have enough votes to clear cloture?
What sticking points remain between the parties?

stories.title: Bitcoin Red Team says AI tools are surfacing critical exploits across core projects
stories.summary: Decrypt reports that the Bitcoin Red Team says AI-based tools have identified critical exploits across a range of core Bitcoin-adjacent projects, in line with a separately reported large-scale AI security sprint across the ecosystem.
stories.whyItMatters: If AI tooling is reliably surfacing critical, previously unknown flaws in core Bitcoin infrastructure, that changes how the ecosystem needs to think about vulnerability discovery and disclosure.
whatToWatch: Which specific projects have confirmed and patched flagged exploits
Whether findings are disclosed responsibly before being made public
questions: Which projects specifically were flagged as having critical exploits?
Have any of these findings been independently verified as genuine?

stories.title: Brazil's central bank orders crypto exchanges to delay large overseas transfers
stories.summary: Brazil's central bank has ordered crypto exchanges operating in the country to delay large transfers sent abroad, according to CoinDesk. The report did not specify the transaction threshold or effective date.
stories.whyItMatters: Capital-flow restrictions on crypto exchanges from a major Latin American regulator signal tightening oversight that could affect how funds move in and out of the country via crypto rails.
whatToWatch: Exchange compliance and any public guidance on the new rule
Reaction from Brazil's crypto industry and possible legal challenges
questions: What transaction size triggers the mandated delay?
Is the rationale capital flight, fraud prevention, or something else?

stories.whyItMatters: This item concerns education policy, not digital-asset markets or regulation, and has no direct bearing on crypto markets or investors.

questions: What is driving the policy change?

stories.title: Bitwise's Matt Hougan predicts trillions in institutional money will flow into Bitcoin
stories.summary: Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan says trillions of dollars in institutional capital are set to flow into Bitcoin, according to CoinDesk. The report did not detail a specific timeline or the basis for the forecast.
stories.whyItMatters: Institutional-adoption forecasts from prominent asset managers shape market narratives, but this is a single executive's projection rather than confirmed flow data and should be weighed accordingly.
whatToWatch: Actual ETF and institutional flow data in coming months as a check on the forecast
questions: What timeline or catalysts underpin the "trillions" figure?
Is this projection tied to any specific policy or market development?
